key_insight: Atomistic stiffness calculations coupled with EBSD-informed finite elements and analytical homogenization reproduce the effective elastic response of polycrystalline NiAl.
engineering_relevance: The framework links crystal-scale elasticity and measured grain structure to bulk stiffness predictions for NiAl engineering components.
method: Compute the single-crystal NiAl stiffness tensor using atomistic calculations.
Build an EBSD-informed 3D polycrystal preserving grain-size and orientation distributions, then simulate uniaxial tension with FEM.
Compare effective elastic properties with experiments and classical analytical homogenization estimates.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports very good FEM–experiment agreement for Young’s modulus and Poisson’s ratio; the Hashin–Shtrikman upper bound and self-consistent approximation closely reproduce experimental Young’s modulus.
watch_item: Agreement depends on the stated modeling assumptions, and the abstract provides no numerical errors to quantify predictive accuracy.
paper_title: Multiscale evaluation of the elastic response of polycrystalline NiAl using molecular statics, EBSD-based finite element and analytical homogenization methods
